correctness.rationale: The full-lattice STAB(P_n) facets x_i≥0 and x_i+x_(i+1)≤1 have primitive normals −e_i and e_i+e_(i+1), which become incidence vectors of a rooted path graph after alternating row signs. Total unimodularity shows simplicial normal cones are smooth. Every minimal dependent active ray set is a root-to-root graph cycle through indices p<q; its endpoint variables zero and all path edge sums one force alternating 0,1,0, giving a local three-coordinate rank-three nonsimplicial cone τ_j, 2≤j≤n−1. Each cone appears and every nonsmooth cone contains one, so the singular support has exactly n−2 irreducible orbit closures Y_j. Fixing x_(j−1)=0,x_j=1,x_(j+1)=0 splits the remaining stable-set face into independent paths, yielding X_(j−2)×X_(n−j−1), of codimension three. The primitive four-ray circuit dual semigroup has four Hilbert generators and equation uv−wz, hence conifold multiplicity two. Joint face intersections are nonempty exactly for nonconsecutive centers, and their toric orbit closures are irreducible, giving Ind(P_(n−2)); unimodularity identifies the singular and non-Q-factorial supports. Independently counted path vertices n=3..8 as 5,8,13,21,34,55 and singular fixed points 1,4,9,17,30,51; these finite checks corroborate, not prove, the all-n graphic-circuit argument.
residual_risks: Only reduced support/generic transverse singularity, not the nonreduced singular scheme or all completed local germs.
Facewise equality of torus-orbit closure intersections depends on the complete normal-fan face order, explicitly used in the proof.

Toric ring normality and Gröbner bases do not imply fan-cone singular incidence. The even-cycle record contains path stable-set varieties as its singular component factors, but does not itself classify singularities of arbitrary path fan X_n. No stronger source was found that entails all n−2 conifolds and Ind(P_(n−2)) arrangement.

value.rationale: A sharp infinite-family toric geometry classification identifies every irreducible reduced singular component, its dimension and product structure, local conifold model, and all higher intersections. For path stable-set polytopes these are natural geometric invariants useful in toric resolutions and adjacent graph families; the theorem is stronger than identifying individual small singular examples.
residual_risks: Does not extend to all trees/cycles and does not compute singular subschemes or arbitrary nongeneric intersection germs.

limitations: All path lengths n≥3, full lattice, arbitrary algebraically closed characteristic, projective normal fan.
Direct independent enumerations checked only n=3..8, not infinite universality.
Other graph/polytope names may hide earlier exact path fan results.
